Overview You can design your own Full Day Customised Kolkata City Tour with stops that match your interests and pace. The tour is private and guided, usually running 7–8 hours with flexible start times between 08:00 and 12:00. You’ll visit iconic landmarks like Victoria Memorial, Howrah Bridge, Marble Palace, and atmospheric spots such as College Street and Mullick Ghat Flower Market. Full Day Customised Kolkata City Tour A Full Day Customised Kolkata City Tour is your own curated journey through India’s cultural capital, built around your schedule and interests. Whether you’re visiting Kolkata for the first time or returning after years, this flexible day trip lets you mix heritage monuments, colonial streets, and local life in one smooth experience. Unlike fixed route sightseeing tours, here you get a private guided customised tour of Kolkata with a dedicated car and local guide. You control the flow: spend more time at the Victoria Memorial or College Street, skip spots you’ve already seen, and even add a short wander around the Maidan or Dalhousie Square if you like. Main highlights of the tour What is this Kolkata city tour all about? This Full Day Customised Kolkata City Tour is designed for guests who want to explore the city at their own rhythm, without feeling rushed. It works especially well for families, couples, solo travelers, and small groups from India, USA, UK, Australia, Canada, France, Italy, Germany, Switzerland, Denmark, Sweden, Singapore, Malaysia, and other countries. The tour is usually a private, guided experience, meaning you travel in a comfortable car with an English speaking guide who understands international travel habits. You can talk about Bengal’s history, literature, food, and daily life while you move between landmarks, coffee houses, and markets that define Kolkata’s spirit. Why choose a customised Kolkata experience? A Customised Kolkata City Tour gives you control over what you see and how long you stay at each place. This is especially useful if you’ve already visited some “must see” spots or want to focus on architecture, food, or street photography. Being a Customised Private Tour, you also avoid noisy group bus itineraries. The same car and guide stay with you throughout the 7–8 hours, so you can ask questions, adjust your route on the fly, and even pause the itinerary for a spontaneous chai or street snack. Main highlights of the tour Iconic colonial architecture – drive past or stop at landmarks like the General Post Office, Town Hall, Raj Bhavan (Governor’s House), High Court, and Writers’ Building, all clustered around Dalhousie Square. Spiritual and humanitarian landmarks – visit the Mother House (Mother Teresa’s mission) and nearby St. John’s Church to understand Kolkata’s role in faith and social service. Cultural and literary heritage – explore Victoria Memorial, College Street, and the Indian Coffee House to feel the city’s legacy in books, debates, and intellectual life. Local daily life at the riverfront – walk through the Mullick Ghat Flower Market and over or near Howrah Bridge, where the city’s commerce and rituals meet the Hooghly River. Grand mansions and heritage homes – step inside the Marble Palace, a 19th century mansion turned museum filled with art, sculptures, and chandeliers that reflect Kolkata’s aristocratic past. Sample itinerary: Your day in Kolkata This is a flexible sample route; you can adjust order, drop stops, or add new ones in coordination with us and your tour guide. Stop At: Mother House Begin with a visit to the Mother House, the headquarters of Mother Teresa’s Missionaries of Charity on Ramkrishna Mission Road. This place gives you a quiet, reflective look at Kolkata’s humanitarian side and the legacy of service connected with the city. Stop At: Mullick Ghat Flower Market Walk along the Mullick Ghat Flower Market on the banks of the Hooghly to see dozens of flower hung boats and stalls. The market is especially vivid in the morning, and it’s a favorite spot for photographers and those who enjoy sensory, local Kolkata. Stop At: Howrah Bridge Pause near Howrah Bridge (Rabindra Setu) to watch pedestrians, bikes, and vehicles cross over the river. The view from the riverfront or the bridge’s side walkways captures the city’s energy and the constant flow of life between Kolkata and Howrah. Stop At: Marble Palace Step inside the Marble Palace, a 19th century mansion built by a wealthy Bengali merchant. The interiors are filled with marble statues, European paintings, and antique furniture, giving you a sense of Kolkata’s colonial era elite culture. Stop At: Victoria Memorial Next, visit the Victoria Memorial, the grand white marble monument and museum in the center of the city. The lawns, galleries, and colonial war time exhibits here make it one of the most recognizable faces of Calcutta City Tour itineraries. Stop At: College Street Stroll through College Street, famous for its rows of second hand and academic bookshops. The area is full of students, researchers, and casual readers, and it offers a lively, bookish atmosphere that feels very “Kolkata”. Stop At: Indian Coffee House Grab a coffee or tea at Indian Coffee House, a retro café that has long been a meeting place for students, writers, and intellectuals. The worn out furniture and constant chatter make it a great place to soak in the city’s youthful, talk heavy vibe. Pass by sights along the route As you move between the main stops, you’ll pass by several iconic landmarks that define Kolkata’s colonial and sporting landscape:• Eden Gardens Stadium – one of India’s most famous cricket grounds.• General Post Office (GPO) – a grand colonial building in Dalhousie Square.• Shaheed Minar – a historic monument formerly known as the Ochterlony Monument.• Akashvani Bhawan and Town Hall – key government and cultural buildings along the route.• Writers’ Building, Raj Bhavan, High Court, Maidan, Race Course, and Fort William – spread across the city center, these form part of Kolkata’s administrative and military heritage.• St. Andrew’s Church and Dalhousie Square – colonial era buildings that frame the official heart of the city. What to expect on the day Tour Start Time Normally the Full Day Customised Kolkata City Tour starts at 09:00 AM, but it can be adjusted to any time between 08:00 AM and 12:00 PM, depending on your preference and hotel location. Tour Duration The tour runs for about 7–8 hours, including stops, travel between locations, and your lunch break. The exact duration can shift slightly if you want longer visits at certain spots. The experience is usually private and guided, with an AC vehicle, and a local guide who can explain history, culture, and lesser known stories of each place. You get to decide the pace—there is no pressure to rush from one site to the next. Lunch and local flavours in Kolkata A scheduled lunch break is built into the Full Day Customised Kolkata City Tour, giving you time to relax and try authentic Bengali or multi cuisine food. The operator will usually suggest 2–3 nearby restaurants where hygiene, variety, and local flavor are balanced. For a true Kolkata experience, you can try: Bengali thali with rice, fish curry, vegetables, and sweets. Paratha or kathi rolls from a popular local eatery. Sandesh, rosogulla, or mishti doi for dessert, all widely available in city restaurants and sweet shops. You’re free to customize your lunch style—vegetarian, non vegetarian, kid friendly, or budget conscious—so discuss preferences with your guide or with us in advance. This customised Kolkata city tour provides the perfect introduction to India’s cultural capital, combining essential historical landmarks with authentic local experiences in a time-efficient format that respects busy travel schedules.
